About the initiative

An HIV learning space grounded in evidence and dignity.

Ruang Tanpa Stigma is an independent digital health education initiative that aims to make HIV information easier to understand, more human and more relevant to people in Indonesia.

Read our editorial policyOpen the educational library

Current status

Ruang Tanpa Stigma is an independent digital health education initiative.

It is not a registered NGO, clinical service, diagnostic provider or emergency service.

Mission

Information that is easier to find, understand and use.

Ruang Tanpa Stigma develops education on HIV basics, testing, prevention, ART, viral load, CD4, PrEP, PEP, U=U, treatment literacy, and supportive, non-stigmatizing communication.

The website is for people seeking HIV information, people living with HIV, people considering testing, partners, friends, family members, students, young adults, and anyone who wants to understand HIV better.

Not written for only one group

Reducing stigma also requires better knowledge across the wider public. We therefore do not write as if every visitor is living with HIV.

HIV does not diminish a person’s worth.

Working principles

Six questions behind every decision.

Is this information trustworthy, human, dignified, clear, privacy-conscious and transparent about its limits?

  • Evidence

    Health information should be accurate, traceable, reviewed and updated when guidance changes.

  • Empathy

    Behind medical terms and health data are people with relationships, choices, experiences and a future.

  • Dignity

    A person’s health status does not determine their worth. Language and design should reflect that respect.

  • Clarity

    Readers should not need medical or public-health training to understand the most important information.

  • Privacy

    The website is designed to collect as little personal information as possible and does not ask for sensitive health data.

  • Transparency

    We distinguish plans, activities, results and impact. Nothing is called successful before it has actually been measured.

How we publish

Warm in language. Rigorous in checking.

Draft → source verification → claim check → language review → clinical/public-health review when required → publication → scheduled review

Indonesia’s Ministry of Health and official health authorities are prioritized for Indonesian context. WHO, UNAIDS and peer-reviewed literature are used as appropriate. External review status is always stated as it actually stands.

An important boundary

Website content provides general education. It does not replace diagnosis, individual risk assessment, medical advice or care from a qualified health professional.
